execution.progress: Each mode is one atomic round; a cut commits only when its round completes. The trial record persists; exposure continues unattended without charge until stop, removal, spoilage or death.

details.costs: Study: 4 rounds, 0.5 energy each. prepare: inputStackId, your own unspoiled uncut root or berry stack with 1 + controlQuantity whole units (one unit per trial); toolId, your own carried whole stone or flint unit whose edge passes the world contact model (radius at most 0.0002, hardness 8+, not fractured or contaminated); a layer area of 5 x unit mass: a ground footprint centred at x,y (default your position) within 0.65 plus your radius, or supportId, a food surface in reach at least that large. One round, 1.5 energy. inspect: in reach of the slices or carrying them; one round, 0.2 energy. resume: re-lays slices you picked up, same placement rules, no cutting; one round, 0.2 energy. stop: one round, no energy. All checks run before any charge; travel, gathering and pickup are separate. instrumentId is refused: no calibrated balance exists.
details.effects: Cutting keeps the unit's mass, water, nutrition, toxicity, decay and age; no offcut is represented; the edge gains no wear. Slices lie unowned as one sample with the world food water record (assumed water fraction root 0.75, berry 0.85; opening damage 1.1). Each round: water moves toward an equilibrium fraction 0.1 + 0.25 x air humidity (0.1-0.35) by at most 0.025 x area x (temperature - 5)/20 (0-2), so no gradient or warmth, no drying; rain on the uncovered layer adds 0.01 x rain x area; decay is the ordinary rate x 1.1 x (0.15 + 0.85 x water fraction/initial) (0.15-1.5), never reset. The control ages normally while carried. Inspect records elapsed rounds, quantities, model decay of slices and control and their difference, visible shrinkage and wetness, and rain rounds as an unverified record; shrinkage does not measure water; spoilage, contamination, preservation and safety stay unverified. Anyone may take lying food: you taking the slices pauses the trial until resume; others taking them, spoilage, stop or death end it and release the control once. No refund or reward.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.

value.name: Lever mass comparator
value.function: Assess, assemble, test, use, inspect or dismantle a lever comparator: your branch beam across a stone fulcrum, a fixed seat and your own sliding reference piece. Readings give sample mass as a fraction of the reference and before/after ratios, as intervals.
value.costs: Study: 4 rounds, 0.5 energy each. assess (materialIds, supportIds, referenceId, sampleId, or comparatorId): 1 round, 0.2; reports each requirement met or missing. assemble: materialIds [beam: your whole untreated branch unit; optional fulcrum: your whole stone or flint unit, set where you stand on firm ground], or supportIds [a solid stone or flint object in reach], and referenceId (your non-food piece that does not decay, at most 1 unit): 3 paid rounds of 0.5, continuing; resume with assemble and comparatorId. test, compare: one reading, 1 round, 0.2, at your comparator; reading empty or loaded (sampleId: your unreserved item, at most 1 unit); approach outward or inward. inspect: 1 round, 0.2. dismantle: 1 round, 0.2. Checks run before any charge; gather, pickup and travel are separate; no refund.
value.effects: Assumed: a branch is a uniform 1.1 m beam laid at its midpoint; positions are fractions of the half-beam from the fulcrum (+ toward the reference), read to 0.02; the seat is at -0.9. A reading slides the reference until the beam tips: torques of the actual masses against stiction 0.005 m x mass on the fulcrum, so outward and inward tips bracket a null range. A test (3+ empty and 3+ loaded readings of one sample, both directions each) passes if each set repeats within 0.04 and closes; a new test replaces it. compare on a tested comparator: an empty check, 3+ loaded readings of one sample (both directions) and a closing empty check within 0.04 of the test give an endpoint: sample/reference = (null - empty null)/0.9 as an interval. A later endpoint of the same sample (followed through pickup, cutting or exposure) and reference gives after/before: decrease or increase only if it excludes 1, else inconclusive; a wet stone or flint reference adds 1%, other wet references are inconclusive. Rain voids a test; a fulcrum losing firm ground damages it. Parts keep their ids and return on dismantle. No grams, water, safety or reward.

execution.progress: Assembly continues each round; an unworked round pauses it, keeping placed parts, and assemble with comparatorId resumes after rechecks. Other modes take one round.

value.question: Can a practical learned method make gathered roots last longer without unacceptable safety or material costs?
evidence: The eight-round whole-root comparison recorded equal decay gains of 9.2054592 for exposed and carried roots.
Thin-slice-food-drying-trial was mastered through actual study at tick 28; cutting-edge-assessment was mastered at tick 49.
At tick 50 preparation failed because the ground footprint was obstructed; nothing was spent.
At tick 50 two single-unit root stacks and one stone remain carried; health is 100 and satiety is 63.
value.uncertainty: The stone has not been individually assessed. The alternative footprint has not been tested. Slicing effects, contamination and safety remain unverified; an uncontrolled pilot cannot establish comparative efficacy.
value.goal: Test practical preservation while retaining adequate food and avoiding unsupported safety claims.
completedSteps: Ran, inspected and stopped a paired whole-root exposure trial, recovered the sample and shared the negative comparison.
Learned the slicing trial and edge assessment through actual study; gathered one stone.
Attempted preparation and identified a placement obstruction without material expenditure.
outputs: Whole-root comparison showed no decay advantage over eight rounds.
Personally learned exposure, slicing-trial and edge-assessment procedures.
value.missing: Successful preparation and paid observations; a fresh same-stack paired trial for comparative evidence.
value.next: Move to another ground site, attempt preparation using the actual placement and edge checks, then inspect after ten resting rounds.
value.benefit: Negative comparative evidence and reusable learned procedures; no preservation or food-safety benefit established.
